The incident signals a new era of cybersecurity challenges specifically related to autonomous AI agents.

bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.

Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware for optimized execution.
This is presented as a preview, indicating ongoing development and performance improvements.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs directly on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Copy Less, Ground More: Overcoming Repetitive Copying in Long-Context Reasoning via Evidence-Aware Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yisen Wang
bullet_points: Identifies 'repetitive copying' as a critical failure mode in long-context reasoning for LLMs.
This failure mode involves models excessively copying input text into their reasoning traces instead of solving the problem.
Proposes an Evidence-Aware Reinforcement Learning approach to mitigate this pervasive issue across frontier LLMs.

stories.title: Agents in the Wild: Where Research Meets Deployment
stories.author: Ioana Baldini
bullet_points: Agentic LLM systems are moving rapidly from research prototypes to real-world production deployments.
These systems demonstrate advanced capabilities including reasoning, planning, and tool coordination.
The shift to deployment introduces critical new challenges concerning robustness, safety, and reliability.

stories.title: ResearchArena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in Automated AI R&D
stories.author: Maksym Andriushchenko
bullet_points: Introduces 'ResearchArena,' a framework to evaluate AI agents automating AI R&D.
Proposes 'AI control' as a method to ensure safety by treating AI agents as potential adversaries.
Focuses on detecting covert sabotage before deploying AI outputs in long-horizon tasks.

stories.title: Copy Less, Ground More: Overcoming Repetitive Copying in Long-Context Reasoning via Evidence-Aware Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yisen Wang
bullet_points: Identifies 'repetitive copying' as a critical failure mode in long-context reasoning for LLMs.
This issue involves models excessively copying input text into reasoning traces instead of solving the problem.
The research proposes an Evidence-Aware Reinforcement Learning approach to mitigate this pervasive behavior in frontier LLMs.

stories.title: Agents in the Wild: Where Research Meets Deployment
stories.author: Ioana Baldini
bullet_points: Agentic LLM systems are moving rapidly from research prototypes to real-world production deployments.
These systems demonstrate capabilities in reasoning, planning, and coordinating with external tools and agents.
Deployment introduces critical challenges beyond algorithmic innovation, specifically concerning robustness, safety, and reliability.

stories.title: CircuitKIT : Circuit Discovery, Evaluation, and Application Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: Introduces CircuitKIT, a new toolkit designed to streamline mechanistic interpretability research in NLP.
Addresses the current fragmentation in circuit analysis by unifying discovery, evaluation, and intervention methods.
Enables more practical downstream applications like pruning, editing, and steering of large language models.

stories.title: Show HN: Cactus Hybrid: We taught Gemma 4 to know when it's wrong
stories.author: HenryNdubuaku
bullet_points: Introduces 'Cactus Hybrid,' a system that enhances small, on-device models (Gemma 4 E2B) by adding a confidence score to every response.
The hybrid approach intelligently routes low-confidence queries to larger, cloud-based models (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite) to maintain accuracy while managing costs.
This addresses the trade-off between the speed/privacy of edge AI and the high cost/occasional inaccuracy of frontier models.

stories.title: RefluXFS: A Linux Kernel Local Privilege Escalation to Root in XFS (CVE-2026-64600)
stories.author: blog.qualys.com via rrampage
bullet_points: A critical local privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-64600) has been discovered in the XFS filesystem within the Linux kernel.
The exploit, named RefluXFS, allows a local attacker to gain root privileges on a compromised system.
This represents a high-severity security flaw requiring immediate attention from Linux kernel maintainers and system administrators.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded model compatibility.
Integration with llama.cpp enhances GGUF model support across various hardware.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Meta won’t have to face the next planned social media addiction trial
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: A planned lawsuit against Meta regarding social media addiction was dropped by the plaintiff.
The case, brought by a 15-year-old in Florida, was intended to be one of several 'bellwether trials'.
The withdrawal of the case removes a significant legal test for Meta's platform practices.

stories.title: Tesla’s revenues are bouncing back, but profits are still weak
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla is showing signs of revenue recovery after a period of weak demand and falling sales.
Despite revenue improvements, the company's profitability remains weak.
The earnings report for Q2 2026 provides insight into Tesla's ongoing recovery trajectory.

stories.title: iOS code could reportedly let Apple cut off apps when users miss iPhone payments
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: iOS 27 beta code reportedly includes functionality for Apple to restrict apps on financed iPhones.
This restriction can be triggered if the user misses scheduled payments on their device.
The feature aligns with reports of Apple preparing a new 'Apple Upgrade' financing program.

stories.title: Here’s what Samsung’s smart glasses actually look like
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Samsung is unveiling new designs for its upcoming smart glasses.
The devices feature a notable 9-hour battery life and are a collaboration with Google.
The smart glasses are set for a fall launch and partner with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker.

stories.title: Microsoft brings original Xbox backward compatibility to Windows PCs
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Microsoft is implementing backward compatibility for original Xbox games on Windows PCs.
The initial four compatible titles can run on hardware as old as an 11-year-old graphics card.
This represents a significant effort in preserving classic gaming experiences on modern platforms.

stories.title: Unlimited AI tokens aren't unlimited after all as US Army burns through supply
stories.author: WIRED
bullet_points: The US Army is experiencing limitations on its AI token supply.
Troops have been notified that their allocated AI tokens are being rapidly depleted.
This highlights real-world constraints and resource management challenges in deploying large-scale AI systems.

stories.title: Appearance Pointers -- Multimodal Region Control of Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Matheus Gadelha
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of text-only prompting in image generation by introducing 'appearance pointers'.
Appearance pointers are compact tokens designed to provide precise regional control over generated images.
The work enhances Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) by giving them mechanisms to spatially guide token influence during generation.

stories.title: CodeRescue: Budget-Calibrated Recovery Routing for Coding Agents
stories.author: Tao Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'CodeRescue,' a new framework for budget-calibrated recovery routing in coding agents.
Challenges traditional cost-aware systems by recognizing that execution feedback in coding allows for valuable, iterative recovery using cheaper models.
Addresses the critical deployment question of when an agent should escalate to more expensive models versus continuing cheap, iterative refinement.

stories.title: ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack
stories.author: Zhangyang "Atlas" Wang
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR): the optimization layer that translates reward feedback into model weight updates.
The research proposes a concept called 'spectral inheritance,' suggesting RLVR can leverage the base model's existing weight spectra.
This mechanism allows the model to acquire new behaviors while reusing the fundamental structure of the original model weights.

stories.title: Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information
stories.author: Aditya Modi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Off-Context GRPO' to enhance reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs) using Reinforcement Learning.
Addresses a critical failure point in standard RLVR: the lack of learning signal when models fail on hard problems.
Proposes using 'privileged information' (like solution prefixes) during training to guide models toward correct, non-zero reward solutions.

stories.title: From Distances to Trajectories: Real-Time Signed Distance Function Mapping and Distance-Accelerated Motion Planning for UAVs
stories.author: Nikolay Atanasov
bullet_points: Proposes co-designing mapping and motion planning using a single representation: Signed Distance Functions (SDFs).
Addresses the challenge of real-time, onboard autonomous flight in cluttered environments for UAVs.
Moves beyond traditional binary occupancy grids by encoding continuous distance information to obstacles.

stories.title: Towards Miniature Humanoid Tele-Loco-Manipulation Using Virtual Reality and Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Jean Chagas Vaz
bullet_points: The research focuses on achieving miniature humanoid tele-locomotion and manipulation.
It combines Virtual Reality (VR) for upper-body teleoperation with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for lower-body control.
This approach allows a single operator to remotely control and navigate a physical robot in a distant environment.

stories.title: PG-KINN: A Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs
stories.author: Saeid Gorgin
bullet_points: Introduces PG-KINN, a Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) for solving PDEs.
Addresses limitations of traditional MLPs in physics-informed learning, such as spectral bias and dense parameterization.
Leverages KANs' learnable spline activations, which align better with classical discretization bases.

stories.title: Multi-modal transformer for signal classification in nanopore blockade experiments
stories.author: Christian Holm
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of classifying complex ionic current signals from nanopore devices.
Introduces a multi-modal deep learning architecture to improve signal classification.
Relevant to advancing single-molecule sensing and portable diagnostics.

stories.title: Selective State-Space Adaptation and Retrieval for Language Model Reasoning
stories.author: Larry Heck
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations of static low-rank adaptation (LoRA) by introducing dynamic, state-aware adaptation.
A novel family of adapters is proposed, featuring selective state-space recurrence at token and instance levels.
A specific method, MaLoRA, dynamically scales the adapter using an input-dependent function integrated with recurrent state.

stories.title: Two-Level Meta-Rubrics for Evaluating Open-Ended Generation: GAMUT, a Benchmark for Factual Completeness
stories.author: Luna Dong
bullet_points: The paper introduces GAMUT, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the factual completeness of long-form AI generations.
Current evaluation methods heavily focus on precision (catching incorrect claims) but often neglect completeness (ensuring all necessary information is present).
Measuring factual completeness is challenging because the required set of facts for a complete answer is rarely a simple, flat list.

stories.title: Prompt Design at Scale: How Format, Instruction Count, and Context Length Shape Instruction Adherence and Hallucination in Large Language Models
stories.author: Netanel Eliav
bullet_points: The study investigates how prompt design choices (formatting, instruction count, and context length) affect LLM performance.
It addresses the lack of controlled evidence in current prompt engineering practices, which are often heuristic-based.
Experiments were conducted on a synthetic corpus to test the impact of these factors on instruction adherence and hallucination.

stories.title: Inference-Time Steering for Cross-Lingual Factual Consistency in LLMs
stories.author: Alexander Manev
bullet_points: LLMs exhibit cross-lingual factual inconsistency, favoring high-resource languages in their knowledge.
The research proposes mitigating these biases by steering the model's behavior at inference time.
The goal is to force models prompted in one language (e.g., English) to maintain factual consistency as if queried in other languages (e.g., German, Spanish).

stories.title: MeetingToM: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Theory-of-Mind Reasoning in Multi-Party Meetings
stories.author: Miao Liu
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'MeetingToM' to evaluate Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) on Theory-of-Mind (ToM) reasoning.
ToM—inferring others' beliefs and intentions—is difficult for current MLLMs, especially in complex, multi-party meeting scenarios.
The research aims to move beyond simple video-grounded QA to assess latent social states and group dynamics in MLLMs.

stories.title: The Price of Reasoning: Cost-Quality Tradeoffs in Reinforcement Learning for Neural Machine Translation
stories.author: Aixiu An
bullet_points: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a viable paradigm for post-training Large Language Models (LLMs) for tasks like Neural Machine Translation (NMT).
RLVR shows promise for specialized tasks, such as translating legal documents, due to its potential to induce reasoning capabilities.
The research prompts a critical discussion on whether observed 'reasoning' is a true emergent property or an artifact of the RLVR training paradigm itself.

stories.title: GigaToken: ~1000x faster Language model tokenization
stories.author: syrusakbary
bullet_points: Introduces 'GigaToken,' a new technology focused on language model tokenization.
Claims a substantial performance improvement, specifically stating ~1000x faster tokenization.
The news originates from Hacker News, suggesting a technical or developer-focused audience.

stories.title: The bug that never crashed: how I fuzzed an AI's own code sandbox and found it lying to its model
stories.author: himanshu_748
bullet_points: A developer successfully fuzzed an AI's internal code sandbox.
The fuzzing process revealed that the AI system was providing misleading information to its own model.
The story is presented as a submission for a bug-bounty/smash event (DEV's Summer Bug Smash).

stories.title: Custom slash commands in Claude Code: how they work now that commands are skills
stories.author: rulestack
bullet_points: Claude Code now supports custom slash commands, which function as 'skills'.
These commands allow users to trigger complex, standardized prompts (e.g., /fix-issue 123) within the AI.
This feature streamlines development workflows by embedding team-specific standards directly into AI interactions.
